flipAftermath.heading: Now you are Ayaan, and it is just gone three
flipAftermath.intro: Ayaan read it between two claims, in the week his team was clearing a backlog. The service desk's own address was on it, and it only asked him to sign in again, which IT had said would happen while single sign-on moved. So he did. That was not carelessness: it was built to pass for the notice he acts on. Here is his account a few minutes later.

items.subject: Updated payment details for your settlement
items.note: Ayaan did not write this; it is in his Sent folder, sent while someone else was signed in as him.
A sign-in prompt he did not start, from a device that is not his.

flipAftermath.line: Most of the damage happens between noticing and reporting.

conceptPanel.heading: The five questions a report answers
conceptPanel.text: A useful report answers five questions, as far as you know: what you noticed, when, where (which account, device or system), who is affected, and what you have done so far. Be honest about the last one: 'I clicked the link', 'I signed in', 'I restarted it'. A rough report now beats a perfect one later; the team will ask for the rest.

conceptPanel.heading: First steps and recovery
conceptPanel.text: If you clicked or signed in: report it, change the password on the real site (not through any link), then change it anywhere you used the same one, and follow the service desk. For anything on a device: leave it as it is. Do not switch it off unless you are told to, do not delete the evidence, and do not try to fix it. If the service desk asks, unplug the network cable or turn off Wi-Fi and leave it on.
